chunks: That no needy person should enter it today among you.

key_terms.الْيَوْمَ: The day (referring to the day of harvest)

ai.seo_question: Who did the people of the garden vow to keep out of their property?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the story of the two sons of Adam or specific companions who hoarded wealth, illustrating how the desire to exclude the 'miskin' (needy) stems from a lack of trust in divine provision. The narrative emphasizes that their vow was not merely economic but a spiritual failure to recognize Allah's sovereignty over sustenance, leading directly to the destruction of their garden as a divine sign.
